title: Tenant-aware sidecollector sync for VPC/on-prem observability and secure sampling
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Dedicated and Private deployments run tenant-proximal collectors (sidecars / perimeter agents) but lack a lightweight, consistent mechanism to synchronize sampling policies, trace headers, and tenant-policing rules across upgrades and transient network partitions. Current workarounds rely on eventual consistency via control-plane push or config polling which leads to sampling drift, incorrect tenant attribution, and occasional high-cardinality tag sprawl in backend traces.

Goal: Implement a tenant-aware sidecollector sync protocol and secure sampling control that: (1) ensures deterministic sampling policy enforcement across sidecars in the same VPC/air-gapped cluster, (2) provides safe fast-rollout and rollback for sampling changes, (3) attaches immutable tenant provenance headers to traces without leaking sensitive metadata, and (4) gracefully handles network partitions and collector restarts with minimal telemetry loss.

Scope: Sidecar agent changes + control plane messaging adjustments. This ticket covers protocol design, agent implementation (sync loop and policy enforcement), mutation-safe rollout, metrics/alerting, and a console dashboard to surface sampling drift and enforcement errors. On-prem installer and firewall considerations included.

Out of scope: Backend storage changes for trace indexing, long-term retention policy, multi-cluster federation beyond single VPC/air-gapped cluster per deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecollector exposes a /policy-check endpoint returning current sampling policy and last-sync timestamp
Control plane can push a sampling update and at least 95% of active sidecollectors in a test VPC report new policy applied within 45s under normal conditions
All emitted traces include tenant_provenance header tokenized (no raw tenant names) and an integrity HMAC header when privacy mode is enabled
Console dashboard shows per-tenant sampling drift metric with historical window and highlights >2% deviation alerts
Chaos test (simulated network partition and sidecar restart) demonstrates eventual reconciliation to latest policy within configured retry window without duplicating traces
implementation_notes: Design protocol as append-only control messages with monotonically increasing version and HMAC-signed payloads for on-prem authenticity
Agent: implement fast-path apply (in-memory) + durable local write for last-good policy to survive restarts
Sampling policy format: allow rate-based + probabilistic + per-route overrides, represented as compact protobuf for wire efficiency
Backoff and jitter: exponential with randomized jitter to avoid stampeding during mass updates
Expose metrics: policy_sync_attempts, policy_sync_success, policy_apply_latency_ms, sampling_enforcement_failures
Provide feature flag to enable tokenized tenant provenance to avoid PII in headers for regulated deployments
risks: Mass rollout could cause short-lived spikes in control plane load; must throttle pushes
Incorrect HMAC key management in air-gapped installs could lead to failed policy validation; need clear KMS/HSM integration guidance
Sampling mismatch may bias observability signals for debugging incidents if not surfaced promptly
Header size growth if tokenization not adopted by downstream consumers
